answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must immediately contact MSHA, without delay and within 15 minutes, at the toll-free number 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred that caused a death of an individual at the mine.

claims.text: Operators must contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes once they know or should know an accident has occurred, including one involving a death.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: Among the triggering accidents listed is a death of an individual at the mine.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in the underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained so its incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: Rock dust must be distributed and maintained so that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust is not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: Where rock dust is required to be applied, it shall be distributed upon the top, floor, and sides of all underground areas of a coal mine and maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The 80 percent minimum is increased only when methane is present, implying 80 percent is the baseline requirement when methane is absent.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device provided to each underground coal miner must be approved and adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: At least once every six months, an underground metal or nonmetal mine must hold evacuation drills.

claims.text: Underground metal or nonmetal mines must hold evacuation drills at least once every six months to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of self-rescue devices.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: This training must be conducted in conditions that as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, with approximately 8 hours given at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: MSHA's noise standard defines the permissible exposure level (PEL) in terms of an 8‑hour time‑weighted average (TWA8) based on a 90‑dB criterion level and a 5‑dB exchange rate used in the noise‑dose formula, with doses then converted to TWA8 readings via a conversion table. The mine operator must ensure that no miner's noise exposure during any work shift exceeds this permissible exposure level, and if it does, must use feasible engineering/administrative controls and enroll the miner in a hearing conservation program. In addition, regardless of hearing protection, no miner may ever be exposed to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA.

claims.text: The mine operator must determine a miner's noise dose using a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate.
claims.quote: Use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate; and

claims.text: The mine operator must use a table when converting from dose readings to equivalent TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) readings.
claims.quote: The mine operator must use Table 62-2 when converting from dose readings to equivalent TWA8 readings.

claims.text: The mine operator must ensure no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise exceeding the permissible exposure level; if exceeded, feasible engineering and administrative controls must be used and the miner enrolled in a hearing conservation program.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise that exceeds the permissible exposure level. If during any work shift a miner's noise exposure exceeds the permissible exposure level, the mine operator must use all feasible engineering and administrative controls to reduce the miner's noise exposure to the permissible exposure level, and enroll the miner in a hearing conservation program that complies with § 62.150 of this part.

claims.text: Regardless of hearing protection, no miner may ever be exposed to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails must be maintained at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. This requirement applies both to surface metal/nonmetal mines (30 CFR 56.9300) and underground metal/nonmetal mines (30 CFR 57.9300).

claims.text: Berms or guardrails at surface metal/nonmetal mines must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails at underground metal/nonmetal mines must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air in an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Mechanisms and procedures must ensure that within the refuge alternative the breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours.
